  SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:00 PM

  Kim Apodaca, Chair
  Rosa Barragan, Vice Chair
  Linda Lopez, Planning Commissioner
  Chris Macias, Planning Commissioner
  Lisa Vernola-Salas, Planning Commissioner

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a
vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.
 CALL TO ORDER

FLAG SALUTE

Commissioner Macias

ROLL CALL OF MEMBERS

MINUTES

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve the minutes of the Special Planning
  Commission meeting of July 22, 2026.

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  For the Planning Commission to consider the following applications continued from the July 22, 2026
  Planning Commission meeting filed by Flores Design Group (Hotel) on property located at 12500
  Firestone Boulevard [also known as Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APN) 8056-011-021], located within the
  Railway Trail District of the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan area pursuant to a Settlement Agreement: (1)
  Precise Development Plan No. 2026-05 to construct an up-to-130 key, four-story hotel on a 1.81-acre lot
  (“Proposed Hotel”) on Parcel B of Tentative Parcel Map No. 85198; and (2) Director Approval Request No.
  2026-11 to allow the establishment and operation of Proposed Hotel. Environmental: Pursuant to the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Addendum to the previously certified Heart of Norwalk
  Specific Plan Environmental Impact Report (EIR) (SCH#2024040140) was prepared for the project
  pursuant to Section 15164 of the CEQA Guidelines. The Proposed Hotel would not result in new
  significant environmental effects or a substantial increase in severity of previously identified significant
  effects.

  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, making a determination that the Proposed
  Hotel development would not result in any new significant environmental effects or a
  substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effects; and

  contained in Exhibit “A” and Mitigation Measures in Exhibit “B”.

agenda was posted at City Hall not less than 72-hours prior to the meeting and forwarded to each member of
the Norwalk Planning Commission on August 7, 2026.

Alexander Hamilton

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  JULY 22, 2026

The meeting was called to order by Chair Apodaca at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Lopez, Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, and Chair
Apodaca. Vice Chair Barragan was absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Deputy City
Manager, John Lam, City Attorney; Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager; Carlos
Rojas, Senior Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of July 8, 2026.

VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO. 2026-04 (85198)
PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2026-05
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2026-11
VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP NO. 2026-04 (84826)
PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2026-03
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2026-05
Brandywine Homes (Residential) and Flores Design Group (Hotel) (“Applicants”) on
property located at 12500 Firestone Boulevard (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number
(“APN”) 8056-011-021), located within the Railway Trail Corridor of the Heart of Norwalk
Specific Plan (“Specific Plan”) area pursuant to a Settlement Agreement.
The project includes requests for:
(1) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 2026-04 (85198) – to subdivide an existing 7.69-
  acre parcel into two parcels. New Parcel A, measuring 5.88 acres in size, is allocated
  for residential development purposes. New Parcel B, measuring 1.81 acres in size,
  is allocated for a new hotel development (“Proposed Subdivision”).
(2) Precise Development Plan No. 2026-05 – to construct an up-to-130 key, four-story
  hotel on a 1.81-acre lot (“Proposed Hotel”) on Parcel B.
(3) Director Approval Request No. 2026-11 – to allow the establishment and operation
  of Proposed Hotel.
(4) Vesting Tentative Tract Map No. 2026-04 (84826) – to subdivide Parcel A into two
  lettered lots for shared access, shared parking, and common landscaping amenities
  and 52 numbered lots for 120 residential condominiums.
(5) Precise Development Plan No. 2026-03 – to demolish an existing 281,661± square
  foot, 230 key hotel and restaurant (Hotel Saddleback) and construct 120 residential
  condominium units on a 5.88-acre lot (Proposed Residential Development) along with
  associated site improvements.
(6) Director Approval Request No. 2026-05 – to allow the use of the Proposed
  Residential Development.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  July 22, 2026

Environmental: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an
Addendum to the previously certified Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan Environmental
Impact Report (EIR) (SCH#2024040140) was prepared for the project pursuant to Section
15164 of the CEQA Guidelines. The Proposed Hotel and Residential Development would
not result in new significant environmental effects or a substantial increase in severity of
previously identified significant effects. The subject property is 12500 Firestone
Boulevard, located northwest of the intersection of Firestone Boulevard and Bloomfield
Avenue.
A copy of the EIR Addendum can be found in the link below:
https://www.norwalk.org/departments_services/community_development/environmental
_documents.php

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas shared that she is going to recuse herself from participating
in this item, and she exited the Council Chambers. City Attorney Lam added that, for the
record, and for an abundance of caution, Commissioner Vernola-Salas may have a
conflict of interest due to a family trust within a 500-foot radius of the subject site.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Rojas presented
a detailed Power Point presentation of the proposed project. He shared that the
entitlements for Precise Development Plan No. 2026-05, to construct an up-to-130 key,
four story hotel on a 1.81-acre lot on Parcel B, and Director Approval Request No. 2026-
11, to allow the establishment and operation of the proposed hotel within the Heart of
Norwalk Specific Plan, is going to be continued to the August 12, 2026, Planning
Commission meeting.

Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Rojas stated that prior to this evening’s meeting, the
Commission received a revised staff report providing information on the 2021-2029
Housing Element contribution, “Housing Element No Net Loss Findings”; that the
Commission also received Revised Resolution No. 26-09; that Condition No. 25 pertains
to the County of Los Angeles Fire Department requirements; and that Condition of
Approval No. 92(d) requires a new drive approach on Front Street; that for background
information, the City Council took action on the Settlement Agreement at their March 17,
2026, meeting for the subject site at 12500 Firestone Boulevard that includes allocation
of a 1.81-acre site for the future development of a hotel on Parcel B.

Further, Mr. Rojas shared that Brandywine Homes is proposing to subdivide Parcel A into
two lettered lots for shared access, shared parking, and common landscaping amenities
and 52 numbered lots for 120 residential condominiums; that after demolishing Hotel
Saddleback, the applicant proposes to construct 50 units designed as single-family units
and 70 three-story townhomes, totaling 120 units; that the primary vehicular ingress and
egress into the proposed residential development is proposed via one 28-foot wide, two-
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  July 22, 2026

way private driveway on Front Street; that the project will provide a total of 275 parking
spaces, consisting of 240 enclosed garage spaces and 35 open stalls for residents and
guests; that the portion of the proposed residential development adjacent to Front Street
will be provided with a total of 23 on-street parking spaces; and that, in addition, an area
serving as a rideshare pick-up zone will be designated within this area.

Next, Mr. Rojas commented on the General Plan and Housing Element indicating that it
is consistent with the General Plan Designation of Specific Plan Area (SPA) No. 18 “Heart
of Norwalk Specific Plan”; that the Housing Sites Inventory identifies the total numbers of
lower income units for the Proposed Residential Development at 229 units resulting in
232 remaining lower income units; that, therefore, it is staff’s assessment that the
remaining sites identified in the City’s Housing Element are adequate to accommodate
the jurisdiction’s share of the regional housing requirements; and that the required “no net
loss finding” is provided in Resolution No. 26-09.

Senior Planner Rojas stated that both the Vesting Tentative Parcel Map and the Vesting
Tentative Tract Map will comply with the State’s Subdivision Map Act; that the Conditions
of Approval for the proposed condominiums require the establishment of a Homeowner’s
Association (HOA), and Conditions, Covenants and Restrictions (CC & R’s) to be
approved by the City Attorney; and that Parkland, Park and Recreation fees are required.
Further, he stated that staff has made findings that the project will not be detrimental to
the public health, safety, and welfare or adversely affect property values or the present
and future development of surrounding areas; and that it is consistent with the purposes
and intent of the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan and with the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Mr. Rojas shared that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission make
the required findings and (1) Adopt the Addendum to the previously certified Heart of
Norwalk Specific Plan Environmental Impact Report (EIR) (SCH#2024040140) pursuant
to Section 15164 of the CEQA Guidelines, making a determination that the Proposed
Residential and Hotel Development would not result in any new significant environmental
effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant
effects; (2) Adopt Revised Resolution No. 26-09, to approve Vesting Tentative Parcel
Map (“VTPM”) No. 2026-04 (85198), Vesting Tentative Tract Map (“VTTM”) No. 2026-04
(84826), Precise Development Plan (“PDP”) No. 2026-03, Director Approval Request
(“DAR”) No. 2026-05 for the Proposed Subdivision and Proposed Residential
Development subject to the revised Conditions of Approval No. 25 and No. 92(d)
contained in Exhibit “A” and Mitigation Measures in Exhibit “B”; and (3) Continue PDP No.
2026-05 and DAR No. 2026-11 for the Proposed Hotel Development to the August 12,
2026, Planning Commission meeting.

In closing, Senior Planner Rojas stated that the continued public hearing of Precise
Development Plan No. 2026-05 and Director Approval Request No. 2026-11 to the
meeting of August 12, 2026, is not subject to any further public notice requirement.

Minutes of the Special Meeting  July 22, 2026

Alex Hernandez, President of Brandywine Homes, stated that he worked with staff for
over a year, and he recognizes their efforts in working with them on resolving all the
various City codes and design standards; that Brandywine has built over 100 homes in
Norwalk and that they have been very successful in their communities in this City.

Sarah Eskandari, Senior Project Manager, Brandywine Homes, stated that she would like
to present a brief recap of the proposed project; that, currently the Hotel Saddleback has
over 200 rooms; that the property consists of 8 acres and 6 buildings; that the appearance
of the hotel looks rather tired and is in need of being refreshed; that they are excited to
bring in a new residential housing development and a future hotel. Further, she showed
slides showing the common area entering the site, the townhome portion and single-
family portion, and she stated that it is a very nicely landscaped community; that the
project will be providing 120 for-sale units and a hotel; that the development will be
generating a little bit over 1.7 million dollars in development impact fees, and that the City
will be benefitting from the future hotel site.

Griffin Joseph, with Unite Here Local 11, presented testimony in opposition to the project.
He stated that this project deviates from the applicable zoning standards and does not
comply with the setbacks and landscaping; that the staff report does not provide
information on the Settlement Agreement; that, to his knowledge, no Development
Agreement has been considered by either the Planning Commission or City Council; and
that Development Agreements, in general, are adopted by an ordinance.

City Attorney Lam shared that a court approved a signed Settlement Agreement which
satisfies the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Apodaca closed
the public testimony.

Commissioner Lopez stated that the renderings of the project shown are beautiful.
Commissioner Macias shared that he is excited to see this new development go in on
that site. Chair Apodaca echoed her fellow Commissioners’ comments and added that
she is looking forward to seeing the project come to fruition.

It was moved by Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Lopez to make the
required findings, and (1) Adopt the Addendum to the previously certified Heart of Norwalk
Specific Plan Environmental Impact Report (EIR) (SCH#2024040140) pursuant to
Section 15164 of the CEQA Guidelines, making a determination that the Proposed
Residential and Hotel Development would not result in any new significant environmental
effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effects;
(2) Adopt Revised Resolution No. 26-09, to approve Vesting Tentative Parcel Map
(“VTPM”) No. 2026-04 (85198), Vesting Tentative Tract Map (“VTTM”) No. 2026-04
(84826), Precise Development Plan (“PDP”) No. 2026-03, and Director Approval Request
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 5
Minutes of the Special Meeting  July 22, 2026

(“DAR”) No. 2026-05 for the Proposed Subdivision and Proposed Residential
Development subject to revised Conditions of Approval No. 25 and No. 92(d) contained
in Exhibit “A” and Mitigation Measures contained in Exhibit “B”; and (3) Continue PDP No.
2026-05 and DAR No. 2026-11 for the Proposed Hotel Development to the August 12,
2026, Planning Commission meeting.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Lopez, Commissioner Macias, and Chair Apodaca
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Vice Chair Barragan

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Planning Commission

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business to come before the Planning Commission, the meeting
was adjourned at 6:44 p.m.

  ________________________________
  KIM APODACA, CHAIR
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION

City of Norwalk City Council adopted its 2021-2029 Housing Element on February 21,
2023. The California Department of Housing & Community Development (HCD) certified
the Housing Element on November 21, 2023. HCD certification was revoked on October
2, 2024 and recertified on September 19, 2025. Since HCD has re-certified the City’s
adopted Housing Element, the City must make certain written findings if the City allows
development on property with a lower residential density than what was assumed in the
City’s Housing Element Sites Inventory (Government Code Section 65863(b)(2)). In
relevant part, “lower residential density” is defined as fewer units on the site than were
projected to be accommodated on the site as described in the Inventory (Government

the requirements of Section 65583.2 and to accommodate the jurisdiction’s share of the
regional housing need pursuant to Section 65584. This finding shall include a
quantification of the remaining unmet need for the jurisdiction’s share of the regional
housing need at each income level and the remaining capacity of sites identified in the
housing element to accommodate that need by income level.

Finding of Fact – The City’s Regional Needs Allocation (RHNA) for the 6th Cycle Housing
Element Update is a total of 5,034 units, which is comprised of 2,305 lower-income units,
658 moderate income units, and 2,071 above moderate-income units. The City’s Housing
Element identified that the City’s residential development capacity is 5,898 total units,
which exceeds the City’s RHNA obligation of 5,034 units by 864 units. This surplus, or
“buffer,” of 864 units is comprised of 612 surplus lower income units, 223 surplus
moderate-income units, and 29 surplus above moderate units.

Since adoption of the 6th Cycle Housing Element Update, the City has approved
entitlements for two projects: a 93‑unit townhome development at 11459 Imperial
Highway and a social services use at 11642 Firestone Boulevard. The Housing Element
Sites Inventory had identified 131 lower‑income units at 11459 Imperial Highway and 20
lower‑income units and 9 moderate‑income units at 11642 Firestone Boulevard.
However, the approved project at 11459 Imperial Highway includes 93
above‑moderate‑income units, resulting in the loss of the 131 lower‑income units
originally anticipated. In addition, the approval of a nonresidential use at 11642 Firestone
Boulevard removes the 20 lower‑income units assumed for that site. As a result, the City’s
surplus buffer of 612 lower‑income units is reduced to 461 units.

The Housing Sites Inventory identifies the total number of units for the subject site (for
both the approved residential project and the proposed hotel) as 229 units, and those
units are projected to consist of 229 lower income units, zero moderate income units, and
zero above moderate-income units. The previously approved Residential Project (VTTM
84826, PDP 2026-03, and DAR 2026-05) proposed 120 above moderate-income
residential units and no moderate- or lower-income units.
As such, since the Subject Site is listed on the sites identified in the Inventory and will
result in the need for the City to deduct 229 lower income units from the City’s surplus
“buffer” of 461 lower income units, resulting in a remaining surplus “buffer” of 232 lower
income units.

Impact – Cultural and Tribal Cultural Resources
MM CUL-1: Historical Built Environmental Studies.
For projects where demolition of structures greater than 50 years is proposed, prior to the issuance of any demolition permits, the
applicant shall prepare an inventory of buildings proposed for demolition located on the project site. The project applicant, under
the direction of the City, shall retain a historian or architectural historian who meets or exceeds the Secretary of the Interior’s
Professional Qualifications Standards to document and evaluate the historical significance of the affected buildings or structures in
accordance with CEQA. If such documentation and evaluation indicate that the building or structure qualifies as a significant
historical resource, the resource shall be avoided, and significant features shall be preserved in place if feasible. If avoidance or
preservation is not feasible, a Historical Resources Treatment Plan, or similar proposed plan, shall be prepared and implemented.
Further documentation may be required and may include, but is not limited to, archival quality photographs, measured drawings,
oral histories, interpretive signage, and/or other measures, including, potentially, alteration of the resource in accordance with the
Secretary of the Interior’s Standards or relocation of the resource.
As defined in the California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 4(3) Section 15126.4 (b)(2), in some circumstances, documentation of a
historical resource, by way of historic narrative, photographs, or architectural drawings, as mitigation for the effects of demolition of
the resource will not mitigate the effects to point where clearly no significant effect on the environment would occur. In these cases,
the Historical Resources Treatment Plan, or comparable plan, shall also evaluate the feasibility of retaining significant buildings or
structures in their original locations and rehabilitating them according to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards and Guidelines for
Rehabilitating Historic Buildings.
MM CUL-2: Archaeological Resource Studies.
Prior to any approval by the City for projects that involve any demolition, grading, trenching, or other ground disturbance, a Phase
I Cultural Resources Study conducted by a qualified archaeologist meeting the Secretary of the Interior standards in archaeology

shall be required. A Phase I study shall include a pedestrian survey of the project site to identify potential surficial archaeological
resources and sufficient background archival research and field sampling to determine whether subsurface prehistoric or historic
remains may be present. If the project site is completely paved and/or developed, a pedestrian survey may not be required. Archival
research should include, at a minimum, a records search conducted at the South Central Coast Information Center (SCCIC) and a
Sacred Lands File (SLF) search conducted with the NAHC of the project site. If the Phase I does not indicate any archeological
resources, no further study is required.
If the Phase I Report indicates potential for important archeological resources that may be eligible for CRHR, a Phase 2 report may
be required if the identified resources cannot be avoided and preserved in place. Where preservation is not feasible, a Phase 2
evaluation for significance and eligibility for listing in the CRHR may be required. The Phase 2 evaluation shall include any necessary
archival research to identify significant historical associations as well as mapping of surface artifacts, collection of functionally or
temporally diagnostic tools and debris, and excavation of a sample of the cultural deposit to characterize the nature of the sites,
define the artifact and feature contents, determine horizontal boundaries and depth below surface, and retrieve representative
samples of artifacts and other remains.
Cultural materials collected from the sites shall be processed and analyzed in the laboratory according to standard archaeological
procedures. The age of archaeological resources shall be determined using radiocarbon dating or other appropriate procedures; lithic
artifacts, faunal remains, and other cultural materials shall be identified and analyzed according to current professional standards.
The significance of the sites shall be evaluated according to the criteria of the CRHR. The results of the investigations shall be
presented in a technical report following the standards of the California Office of Historic Preservation publication “Archaeological
Resource Management Reports: Recommended Content and Format (1990 or latest edition)”. Upon completion of the work, all
artifacts, other cultural remains, records, photographs, and other documentation shall be curated at an appropriate curation facility.
All fieldwork, analysis, report production, and curation shall be fully funded by the applicant.
If any of the resources meet CRHR significance standards, the City shall ensure that all feasible recommendations for mitigation of
impacts are incorporated into the final design and any permits issued for development. Any necessary archaeological data recovery
excavation shall be carried out by a Registered Professional Archaeologist according to a research design reviewed and approved by
the City prepared in advance of fieldwork and using appropriate archaeological field and laboratory methods consistent with the
California Office of Historic Preservation Planning Bulletin 5 (1991), Guidelines for Archaeological Research Design, or the latest
edition thereof.
As applicable, the final Phase 1 Inventory, Phase 2 Testing and Evaluation, Phase 3 Data Recovery reports shall be submitted to the
City prior to final inspection of a construction permit.
Recommendations contained therein shall be implemented throughout all ground disturbance activities, including, at a minimum,

MM CUL-3: Unanticipated Discovery of Human Remains.
Consistent with the regulatory provisions to address the handling of human remains in California Health and Safety Code § 7050.5,
PRC § 5097.98, and State CEQA Guidelines § 15064.5(e), in the event that human remains are discovered, it requires that disturbance
of the site shall be suspended, encountered during site disturbance, grading, or other construction activities on the project site, the
construction contractor shall halt work within 25 feet of the discovery. The Project Applicant shall immediately notify the City of
Norwalk and the Los Angeles County Coroner. The coroner shall conduct an investigation into the circumstances, manner, and cause
of any death, and the recommendations concerning the treatment and disposition of the human remains have been made to the
person responsible for the excavation or to his or her authorized representative, in the manner provided in § 5097.98 of the PRC. The
coroner is required to make a determination within two working days of notification of the discovery of the human remains. If the
coroner determines that the remains are not subject to his or her authority and if the coroner recognizes or has reason to believe the
human remains to be those of a Native American, he or she shall consult with the NAHC by telephone within 24 hours to designate
a Most Likely Descendant (MLD) who shall recommend appropriate measures to the landowner regarding the treatment of the
remains. If the owner does not accept the MLD’s recommendations, the owner or the MLD may request mediation by the NAHC.

may recommend alternative procedures that produce lower vibration levels, such as sonic pile driving or caisson drilling instead of
impact pile driving. Development projects shall implement the structural engineer’s recommendations.
A Statement of Compliance signed by the Applicant and Owner is required to be submitted to Building and Safety at plan check and
prior to the issuance of any permit. The Vibration Control Plan, prepared as outlined above, shall be documented by a qualified
structural engineer and shall be provided to the City upon request.
